name: Escitalopram + Clonazepam
meta: Schedule H – prescription only; Clonazepam: Psychotropic substance under the NDPS Act, 1985 and Schedule H/H1 of the Drugs & Cosmetics Rules
sections: Fine white to slightly yellow powder (oxalate), sparingly soluble in water.
Off-white to light yellow crystalline powder, insoluble in water.

Escitalopram Oxalate: The therapeutically active S-enantiomer of citalopram; approved for major depression in 2002 and generalised anxiety disorder in 2003. First approval/introduction: US FDA August 2002 (Lundbeck / Forest Laboratories). Clonazepam: One of the Roche 1,4-benzodiazepines; widely used for seizure disorders and panic disorder. First approval/introduction: Patented 1960, marketed 1964; US FDA 1975 (Roche).

SSRIs take 2–4 weeks to act and may initially worsen anxiety/jitteriness. Clonazepam provides immediate anxiolytic and anti-panic effect during this lag phase. Dependence risk makes long-term use of the fixed combination inadvisable.

Escitalopram Oxalate S-enantiomer of citalopram; the most selective SSRI. Inhibits serotonin reuptake at the presynaptic transporter, with allosteric binding that prolongs transporter blockade. Receptor / target profile: The most SERT-selective SSRI, binding both orthosteric and allosteric sites (Ki 0.8–1.1 nM); negligible NET/DAT activity.

Clonazepam Enhances GABA-A receptor-mediated inhibitory neurotransmission; has potent anticonvulsant and anti-panic activity and some serotonergic effects. Receptor / target profile: Binds the benzodiazepine site of GABA-A receptors, increasing the effect of GABA; also has serotonergic activity.
Summary: Bioavailability ~80%; Tmax ~4 h. ~56% protein bound. Metabolised by CYP2C19, CYP3A4 and CYP2D6. Half-life ~27–32 h.
Hepatic – CYP3A4 nitro-reduction to 7-aminoclonazepam, then acetylation
Summary: Bioavailability ~90%; Tmax 1–4 h. ~85% protein bound. Metabolised by CYP3A4 (nitro-reduction). Half-life 30–40 h.
Short-term management of depression or panic disorder with marked anxiety, where rapid anxiolysis is needed during the SSRI onset period
Generalised anxiety disorder with insomnia/agitation (initial phase)
One tablet once daily, preferably at bedtime
Use the combination for the shortest period (usually 2–4 weeks), then continue escitalopram alone and taper clonazepam
Dose to be individualised by the treating physician according to clinical response and tolerability.
Approved for MDD (12–17 y) and GAD (≥7 y) in some regions; monitor for suicidality.
Use only if clearly needed; neonatal adaptation syndrome and PPHN possible with late exposure.
Excreted in breast milk; breastfeeding not recommended.
Seizures: 0.01–0.03 mg/kg/day initially; hypersalivation; behavioural effects.
Avoid; risk of neonatal sedation and withdrawal.
Known QT prolongation or congenital long QT syndrome
Dose-dependent QT prolongation (max 10 mg/day in elderly)
Dependence, abuse and withdrawal – use lowest effective dose for shortest time; taper
MAOIs, linezolid, triptans, tramadol, lithium (serotonin syndrome)
Alcohol, antihistamines, antipsychotics, other CNS depressants
Escitalopram Oxalate: With or without food; avoid alcohol.
Clonazepam: Avoid alcohol and grapefruit juice.
Escitalopram Oxalate: QTc in patients with cardiac risk; sodium in elderly; mood/suicidality during first weeks.
Clonazepam: Sedation, respiratory function, dependence; LFTs and CBC on long-term therapy.

Escitalopram Oxalate: Dizziness, tremor, agitation, somnolence, seizures, QT prolongation, serotonin syndrome. Supportive care with ECG monitoring. Clonazepam: Somnolence, confusion, ataxia, hypotonia, respiratory depression, coma. Supportive care; flumazenil with caution.
Goddard et al., Arch Gen Psychiatry 2001 – adding clonazepam to an SSRI (sertraline) produced faster response in panic disorder.
Smith et al., Am J Psychiatry 1998 – fluoxetine plus clonazepam gave earlier improvement in depression.
Initial anxiety or nausea may occur – usually temporary
Store below 30°C in a dry place, protected from light and moisture. Keep out of the reach of children. Do not use after the expiry date.
